edits.content: Before ranking options, verify each distinguishing clause independently; choose the strongest claim actually supported, not the strongest-sounding one. An existential example does not establish a universal bound; a range of possible parameter values does not establish that every value is realized; existence of a solution does not establish least energy; and a named decomposition or kernel dimension does not by itself establish additional non-symmetry fields. Treat words such as “every,” “all,” and “conversely” as added quantifiers requiring evidence. Preserve whether the question asks for an existence claim or a universal one, and compare options only after checking their exact conclusions.

Check algorithmic and probabilistic clauses independently: a decision algorithm need not construct witnesses, and almost-sure convergence to one member of a list plus positive probability for one specified limit does not imply probability zero for the others. Claims of positive probability, probability zero, and “for every” index require direct support. Replacing a joint AND hypothesis by OR weakens the premise and therefore makes the conclusion a stronger theorem; do not make that substitution without evidence.

For PDE claims, inspect the actual system structure before importing intuition from a scalar equation: check reaction signs, coupled components, and conserved combinations before predicting blow-up or global existence. In weak elliptic formulations, distinguish data orders carefully: if F is only in L², div F is generally distributional H⁻¹ data, not L² data, and an L¹ source is not L²; do not claim H² regularity from an L²-data estimate without additional hypotheses.

For integer divisibility criteria, derive the exact scaling from the stated theorem or transformation and preserve it: d | ℓ, d | 2ℓ, and ℓ | d are different conditions. Do not infer or discard a factor of 2 merely from wording such as “2ℓ twists.”

A rational parametrization in a parameter and fixed geometric data does not imply invariance or allow the parameter to be eliminated. Eliminate a parameter only when constancy on the actual admissible parameter set is established; do not replace that set by a larger domain without justification.

For an equivalence, check both directions. For case splits or counting conditions, compare each branch literally, including equality versus strict inequality, allowed index classes, and exactly one versus at most one. Keep local or per-degree existence distinct from a globally coherent or multiplicative family.

For growth exponents defined by a liminf, translate the claim into counting inequalities before comparing options. If liminf as N tends to infinity of log A(N) / log N is at least alpha, then for every epsilon > 0, eventually A(N) >= N^(alpha - epsilon); this does not necessarily imply A(N) >= c N^alpha for a fixed c > 0. Check endpoint exponents and constant-factor claims separately.
